about: Every golden and pin, with the kind of reason it deserves trust and the evidence for that reason. Kept honest by tools/golden_registry_check.py (B448 P8, ADR-209). `independent` is true only when a recorded closed form, listening sign-off or measurement was found and is cited. An honest low count is the point of this file.
open_rulings: Bit-identity pins and self-digest references are counted as goldens here. That is the lead's reading of docs/strategy/blind-spot-armor-phase2.md section 7 ('Do bit-identity pins count as goldens under S2?', recommend yes, registered as prototype parity at pin, sign-off pending). The human has not ruled on it.

tests/morph_order.txt is a compatibility freeze (saved sessions read it by slot position). The four kinds do not name that justification, so it sits as prototype_parity_at_pin, not independent. Whether it needs a fifth kind is the human's to rule.

kinds.closed_form: the expected value follows from mathematics, independent of our code
kinds.prototype_plus_signoff: parity with the JS prototype AND a recorded listening sign-off by the human
kinds.measurement: a measured number with its method recorded, judged by a tolerance or regime rather than by byte equality with code output
kinds.prototype_parity_at_pin: matches the prototype or the code as of the day it was pinned, and nothing more; sign-off pending

known_limits: Generators are registered as the golden: the rendered files live in build-golden/ at verify time and are never committed (ADR-187 item 7).

Pinned numbers embedded in check sources are found only where the scenario-floor marker tokens appear (see RULES, FLOOR). Other literals (kMinBank in preset_pitch_check, kLayoutPins in morphlayout_check, per-check tolerances) are not discovered by this tool; tolerances are covered by docs/armor/tolerances.json.

Closed-form checks that keep their expectations in code (svf_check and twocluster_check, which blind-spot-armor-phase2.md section 1 row R10 names as prototype-independent) hold no golden file and are not listed. The closed-form suite is P7.
A measurement is credited only when it is a recorded number with its method, judged by a tolerance or regime. A byte-for-byte snapshot of the code's own probe output is not.

A reviewer may reasonably ask for this to be demoted; the rule used is in known_limits.
